features.title: Project scaffolding, configuration, Docker Compose Postgres 16, and health server
acceptance_criteria: Rust crate `maxi-loop` builds cleanly with `cargo check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and `cargo build`
Centralized env config validates all fields and redacts `DATABASE_URL` in Debug output
`docker-compose.yml` starts isolated PostgreSQL 16 on localhost port 55432 with `.env` gitignored
`GET /healthz` and `GET /api/v1/health` verify Postgres connectivity with timeout and return safe status JSON without leaking internals
Embedded React (Vite + TS + Tailwind) SPA builds cleanly and is served from the single Rust binary with security headers
PRD and design documents are stored under `docs/` and `.harness/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `decisions.md` are populated

features.title: PostgreSQL schema, daily-partitioned events, RLS tenant isolation, and bootstrap CLI
acceptance_criteria: SQLx migrations create tenants, workspaces, projects, users, memberships, sessions, issues, daily-partitioned events, and issue_hourly_counters with tenant_id + project_id leading keys/indexes
Row-Level Security policies enforce tenant isolation via `app.tenant_id` per transaction alongside a dedicated worker DB role
First-boot/CLI bootstrap creates default tenant, default workspace, and initial admin user cleanly (idempotent)
Integration tests verify migrations, partition creation, and RLS isolation against Postgres 16

features.title: Session auth (Argon2id + CSRF) and Tenant/Workspace/Project/DSN management API
acceptance_criteria: Login/logout/me endpoints use Argon2id password hashes, CSPRNG session tokens, HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, CSRF protection, and login rate limiting
Admin/tenant API creates and lists workspaces, projects, and generates/rotates project DSNs with slug-based routes
Single-tenant mode flag exposes default tenant/workspace seamlessly
Automated cross-tenant isolation tests verify Tenant A cannot read or mutate Tenant B resources
features.notes: PRD F-ADM-1, F-ADM-2, F-ADM-6, F-ADM-7, F-ADM-10

features.title: Sentry Envelope ingest endpoint with DSN cache, decompression, rate limiting, and bounded channel
acceptance_criteria: `POST /api/{project_id}/envelope/` authenticates DSN from in-memory cache without per-envelope DB queries
Supports gzip, deflate, and brotli request decompression with enforced body/event size limits
Drops unsupported item types (session, replay, profile, attachment) early
Per-project `governor` rate limit and full-channel backpressure return HTTP 429 with Retry-After / X-Sentry-Rate-Limits headers

features.title: Ingest worker pool: default PII scrubbing, fingerprinting, issue upsert/reopen, capped events, batch insert
acceptance_criteria: Worker scrubs default sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) and fields (password, token, secret, api_key) before persistence
Fingerprint grouping hashes exception type + in-app stack frames (with error message fallback)
Batch writer flushes every 100ms-1s: upserts issues, auto-reopens resolved issues on regression, caps full payloads at configured max (default 50) + sample, and increments hourly counters
Unit and integration tests cover grouping consistency, regression reopen, PII scrubbing, and event cap
features.notes: PRD F-ISS-1, F-ISS-4, F-ISS-5, D002 baseline PII scrubbing; Design §5.2-5.4

features.title: Issues query, detail, hourly stats, and triage JSON API with tenant isolation tests
acceptance_criteria: List issues supports pagination and filters by project, environment, release, and status
Issue detail returns summary, stack trace, tags, environment, release, sample event, and hourly/daily counter series
Issue status endpoint updates unresolved/resolved/ignored with server-side authorization
Cross-tenant isolation tests verify Tenant A cannot access Tenant B issues, events, or stats

features.title: Retention scheduler: daily partition maintenance, DROP PARTITION, and override batch delete
acceptance_criteria: Background scheduler pre-creates upcoming daily partitions and drops partitions older than global retention (default 30 days)
Workspace/project retention overrides are validated `<= global` and cleaned via bounded scheduled batch deletes
Integration tests verify partition creation, dropping expired partitions, and shorter override cleanup

features.title: Embedded React UI: Login, Projects & DSN, Issues list/detail, and hourly chart
acceptance_criteria: Login view authenticates via session cookie and hides tenant/workspace chrome in single-tenant mode
Projects view lists/creates projects and displays copyable Sentry DSN
Issues list supports filters (project, environment, release, status) and pagination
Issue detail shows stack trace, tags, sample event payload, hourly trend chart, and resolve/ignore/reopen actions
`npm --prefix web run build` succeeds and embeds into the Rust binary

features.title: Envelope load-test generator and real Python (Django/FastAPI) Sentry SDK E2E verification
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic envelope generator benchmarks ingest throughput and 429 behavior against running server
Official Python `sentry-sdk` (FastAPI/Django) successfully reports grouped exceptions by only changing DSN
Baseline throughput and idle RSS measurements are documented

features.title: Phase 2: Configurable PII scrubbing, Release tracking, and Alerts (Webhook, Telegram, Email)
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant/workspace/project PII scrub rules applied in ingest worker
Release tracking links issues and events to releases
Alert engine triggers on new issue, regression, or spike with Webhook first, then Telegram and Email

features.title: Phase 2b: Embedded MCP server (/mcp Streamable HTTP) for AI issue analysis and triage
acceptance_criteria: Streamable HTTP `/mcp` endpoint runs over the shared internal service layer with revocable scoped Bearer tokens (`read` default, `triage` opt-in)
Implements `list_projects`, `list_issues`, `get_issue`, `get_event`, `get_issue_stats`, `update_issue_status`, `add_issue_note` with token-efficient output and release-to-SHA mapping
Wraps untrusted event content, scrubs PII on output, enforces per-token rate limit, writes audit logs, and passes cross-tenant isolation tests

features.title: Phase 3: Performance monitoring (transactions, spans, histograms, sampled zstd traces, waterfall, MCP tools)
acceptance_criteria: Ingests transactions and spans, aggregates 1-minute duration histograms for p50/p95/p99, throughput, and error rate
Stores sampled full traces (slow, error, 1-5% random) compressed with zstd and renders distributed trace waterfall
Exposes `list_transactions` and `get_trace` via UI API and MCP

features.title: Phase 4: React Source Maps upload per release and bounded LRU ingest-time resolution
acceptance_criteria: Source maps can be uploaded per release (matched by release + filename or debug id)
Ingest worker resolves minified JS stack frames using a bounded LRU cache before fingerprinting

features.title: Phase 5: Go & Rust SDK verification, multi-user RBAC, inherited settings, API tokens, aggregate tenant limits
acceptance_criteria: Verified error and trace ingestion with official Go and Rust Sentry SDKs
Multi-user RBAC (`tenant_owner`, `tenant_admin`, `workspace_admin`, `member`, `viewer`), inherited settings, per-project API tokens, and aggregate tenant rate limits

features.title: P2 Issues: Manual issue merge/split (with fingerprint alias routing) and event breadcrumbs viewer
acceptance_criteria: Manual merge combines source issues into a target issue within the same project (events, hourly counters, releases, notes, alert deliveries) and routes future events with merged fingerprints to the target issue
Manual split detaches merged fingerprints or selected stored events into standalone issues, updates counters/releases/sample events, and restores independent routing for split fingerprints
Event breadcrumbs (HTTP, navigation, UI, query, console, custom) are normalized and rendered in issue detail, stored events viewer, and API responses with PII scrubbed
RBAC, same-project validation, API token write/project scoping, and cross-tenant isolation are enforced and tested against PostgreSQL 16

features.title: P2 Performance & MCP: Compare releases, slow DB queries/operations aggregation, MCP list_slow_queries/compare_releases & prompt templates
acceptance_criteria: Aggregates slow DB queries and operations per normalized op and description (p50/p95/avg/count/total_ms) from ingested transaction spans
Compares two releases for a project across performance percentiles, throughput, error rate, and issue counts
Exposes `list_slow_queries` and `compare_releases` MCP tools and MCP prompt templates (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`) for issue triage and fixing
Renders Compare Releases and Slow Queries UI in MaxiBoard Performance view and passes cross-tenant isolation tests

features.title: Performance Issues: detect N+1 DB, N+1 API, Slow DB Query, Consecutive DB/HTTP from transaction spans and surface them as issues
acceptance_criteria: Every ingested transaction (sampled or not) runs span detectors with Sentry-like thresholds: N+1 DB (>=5 identical normalized queries, >=50ms total), N+1 API (>=5 identical normalized http.client calls, >=100ms), Slow DB Query (single query >=1s), Consecutive DB (>=2 sequential sibling queries >=30ms each, savings >=100ms), Consecutive HTTP (>=3 sequential calls >=500ms each, savings >=1s)

Each detected problem becomes an issue in the existing `issues` table with `issue_type` (migration 0011), grouped by type + transaction + normalized pattern, reusing regression, releases, hourly counters and alerts
Transactions that trigger a detector are always kept as sampled traces (`sample_reason = 'issue'`) and linked from the issue
Performance issue payloads only contain normalized (literal-free) span descriptions
Issues API + MCP `list_issues` support `issue_type` filter (`error`, `performance`, exact type); merge across different issue types is rejected
UI: Type filter + PERFORMANCE lozenge in Issues list; drawer and full view show the offending spans and open the trace waterfall
Verified E2E with official Python sentry-sdk + Django (`tests/e2e/python/verify_performance_issues.py`)
features.notes: Sentry detects performance issues server-side; SDKs only send spans. Probe on 2026-11-22 showed Maxi Loop captured all errors but no performance issues.

features.title: Users affected per issue and impact-based sorting
acceptance_criteria: Ingest derives a hashed user identity from event `user` (id / email / ip) without storing raw PII for the count
Issues list/detail show distinct users affected; issues can be sorted by users
Spike alerts can use user counts in addition to event counts
features.notes: Agreed with user 2026-11-22 as high-value follow-up. Done 2026-11-22: migration 0012, keyed tenant-scoped user hash (D010), sort=users, spike_metric=users. The Python SDK strips user.ip_address unless send_default_pii=True, so IP-only users are only counted when the SDK sends the IP.

features.title: Performance alerts: p95 latency and error-rate thresholds per transaction/project
acceptance_criteria: New alert rule types for p95 > X ms and error_rate > Y% on a transaction or project, evaluated every minute from `transaction_minute_metrics`
Delivered via existing webhook / Telegram / email channels with cooldown deduplication and audit log
features.notes: Agreed with user 2026-11-22 as high-value follow-up. Done 2026-11-22: migration 0013, D011. Deliveries with status 'failed' do not start a cooldown (same as issue alerts), so a failing channel is retried every tick while the condition holds.

features.title: Optional ingest spool file: crash-safe on-disk write-ahead log for accepted envelopes
acceptance_criteria: `INGEST_SPOOL_DIR` unset = unchanged behaviour; set = every accepted envelope is appended to a CRC-checked segment file before it is queued
Worker persists a checkpoint after each flushed batch; fully checkpointed segments are deleted; active segment fdatasync'd every second
On startup, records after the checkpoint are replayed to the worker before HTTP is served; torn/corrupt tails are skipped
Channel full still returns 429 without writing; spool write failure returns 503
Spool dir 0700 / files 0600 (raw unscrubbed payloads), refuses group/other-accessible dir, exclusive lock file, bounded record size
Unit + integration tests and a kill -9 smoke test with the real binary show no accepted event is lost
features.notes: Agreed with user 2026-11-22 (production packaging moved to the end). PRD §8 / design §5.2 spool file. Done 2026-11-22: D012 (segments rotate at 64 MiB or 30 s, checkpoint after each batch, at-least-once). MSRV raised to 1.89 for File::try_lock. E2E SIGKILL test: 1200 accepted, 210 replayed, 0 lost, 0 duplicates.

features.title: Phase 2 load test: transaction/mixed loadgen modes and benchmark report
acceptance_criteria: `maxi-loop-loadgen --kind error|transaction|mixed`; transaction envelopes carry realistic spans incl. N+1 DB patterns
Benchmarks on the current release: idle/peak RSS, HTTP throughput & latency, sustained persistence rate, 429 behaviour, with and without INGEST_SPOOL_DIR
Results and reproduction steps in docs/benchmarks-phase2.md; no accepted event lost
features.notes: Agreed with user 2026-11-22 (after F020; production packaging last). Done 2026-11-22: loadgen --kind error|transaction|mixed + bench_phase2.py + docs/benchmarks-phase2.md. 240,600 accepted envelopes across 8 runs (no-spool & spool), 0 lost, 0 5xx; idle RSS 12.0 MiB, peak RSS 115.3 / 106.0 MiB, sustained persist 3.67k err / 3.22k tx / 2.22k mixed items/s (spool overhead 0.5%–3.2%).

features.title: Invite-by-link member onboarding
acceptance_criteria: Admins with member-management rights create single-use invite links (7-day expiry) for an email + role + tenant/workspace scope; same privilege rules as direct member creation
Only the SHA-256 of the 256-bit token is stored; the raw link is shown once; token travels in the URL fragment
Invitee previews the invite and either creates an account (name + own password) or proves an existing account's password, then is signed in
Pending invites listed and revocable per scope; re-inviting replaces the old link; expired/revoked/used links are rejected
features.notes: Done 2026-11-22 (D015). Email delivery of the link is not implemented: admin copies the link. Direct creation with admin-set password kept as 'Create directly'.

features.title: Self-service password change
acceptance_criteria: Signed-in user changes password after verifying the current one (12-256 chars, Argon2id)
All other sessions of the user are revoked; current session stays
Rate-limited; wrong current password -> 403
features.notes: Done 2026-11-22. Forgot-password/reset by email not implemented (needs email delivery).

features.title: Issue assignment (UI + MCP)
acceptance_criteria: One optional assignee per issue; triage-capable callers can assign/reassign/unassign; viewers and read-only tokens cannot
Only active members who can triage the issue's project are assignable (SQL `user_can_triage_project`, single rule shared by API, list and trigger)
Assignment changes recorded on the issue timeline; removed/downgraded members are auto-unassigned (trigger)
Issue list filter `assigned_to=me|none|<user id>|<email>`; assignee shown in list, drawer and full view
MCP: `assign_issue` ('me' | email | null) and `list_assignable_members` (triage scope), `assigned_to` filter on `list_issues`, assignee in `list_issues`/`get_issue`; triage prompt suggests assignment
features.notes: Done 2026-11-22 (D016). Stage B (per-member project access, invite project picker) agreed as next step: tighten `user_can_triage_project`. Auto-unassign by trigger does not write a timeline note. No assignee notification yet.

features.title: Workspace isolation hardening (B0)
acceptance_criteria: Users with workspace-scoped access cannot read or change other workspaces' data via issues (lists, stats, events, notes), performance, releases, source maps, alert channels/rules/deliveries, PII rules or MCP
List endpoints filter visible projects in SQL (correct totals/pagination)
MCP tokens can only be created for scopes the creator can access/triage; role is recomputed inside the token scope on every request; tenant-wide MCP token/audit listing only for tenant owners/admins
Negative test for every hole, verified failing on the pre-fix code
features.notes: Done 2026-11-22 (D017). Test crates/server/tests/b0_workspace_isolation.rs. Prepares Stage B (per-project access): all checks go through AuthSession::project_access / can_read_project / AccessGuard.

features.title: Per-member project access (Stage B)
acceptance_criteria: Workspace member/viewer memberships and invitations can be limited to selected projects of that workspace (empty selection = all projects)
Limits apply to every project-data path (lists in SQL, single records, performance, MCP tokens, assignment eligibility)
Deleting the last allowed project never widens access (explicit project_limited flag)
Only workspace managers can change limits; promotion to workspace_admin clears them; narrowing unassigns issues the member can no longer triage
UI: project picker when adding/inviting, editable project access per member, limits shown in members/invitations and on the accept page

features.title: Production packaging and deploy (loop.maxiflow.id)
acceptance_criteria: Multi-stage Dockerfile (npm build -> cargo release -> Debian slim), non-root runtime user, 0700 spool dir
docker-compose.prod.yml: PostgreSQL 16 (not published) + app on 127.0.0.1 only, read-only rootfs, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, capped logs, spool volume
nginx vhost with TLS (certbot) behind Cloudflare Full, real client IP only from Cloudflare ranges
deploy/deploy.sh ships the image over SSH with rollback tag and /healthz wait; deploy/README.md covers one-time setup, admin bootstrap, rollback, backup
Live at https://loop.maxiflow.id: /healthz 200, admin login works, anonymous API 401
features.notes: Done 2026-11-23 (D019). Secrets (.env, ADMIN_CREDENTIALS) exist only on the server in ~/maxi-loop (0700/0600).

features.title: Ingest large span-heavy transactions so N+1 requests are detected like Sentry
acceptance_criteria: `transaction` items have their own cap MAX_TRANSACTION_PAYLOAD_BYTES (default 2 MiB); error events keep MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES (512 KiB); MAX_ENVELOPE_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES default 3 MiB; startup fails if an item cap exceeds the envelope cap
Every 413 from an authenticated DSN is logged as WARN with tenant, project, size and reason
Up to 1000 spans per transaction are analyzed (Sentry SDK default max_spans)
Span grouping hashes the full normalized description (input bounded to 8192 chars); stored text keeps head and tail so WHERE stays visible
Performance issue titles collapse ORM column lists: `SELECT .. FROM table WHERE ...`
Real Django app (personalia): N+1 on 6 endpoints with up to 1000 spans / 1.4 MB per transaction all become issues with default config
features.notes: Done 2026-11-24 (D020). Long-SQL span groups get new hashes (short queries unchanged).

features.title: Event context like Sentry: browser, OS, runtime, request, SDK on issues
acceptance_criteria: Browser and client OS are derived server-side from the request User-Agent when the SDK does not send them (contexts.browser / contexts.client_os), like Sentry
Error and performance issue events get Sentry-style tags: browser, browser.name, client_os, client_os.name, os, os.name, runtime, runtime.name, device, server_name, url (existing SDK tags win)
Performance issue events carry a bounded, already-scrubbed snapshot of the transaction's request (method, url, query string, headers; no body), contexts (no trace/profile), sdk and server_name
Issue drawer and full view show a Context panel (Browser, OS, Runtime, Device, Request, SDK, Server) for both error and performance issues
Unit tests for UA parsing, tag derivation and snapshot bounds; workspace tests, fmt, clippy and web build pass

features.title: Regressions menu and Issues tabs stay in sync (menu, tab, title, reload, Back)
acceptance_criteria: Sidebar Regressions = Issues view on the Regressed tab; the URL `status` is the only source of truth for the tab
Sidebar highlight follows the tab (Regressed tab -> Regressions, other tabs -> Issues); title shows Regressions on that tab
Reload keeps the chosen tab (no jump back to Regressed); Back/Forward between Issues and Regressions works; old `view=regressed` links still open Regressions
Regressions empty state explains what a regression is
